title: altdown 0.0.0.9000
text:
Writes altdoc/altdown.yml, the configuration file build_site() reads. It starts with a reference: field listing every function currently documented in <path>/man/*.Rd in one "All functions" section. Also adds the .gitignore/.Rbuildignore entries the build needs (see Details) if they’re not already there.



use_altdown(path = ".")






path


Path to the target package root. Defaults to the current directory.






An existing altdoc/altdown.yml is never overwritten. If the package was set up with an earlier version of altdown, the reference: field is taken over from its altdoc/reference.yml; that file, and the altdoc/build-site.R and altdoc/quarto_website_static.yml copies, are no longer used and can be deleted.
use_altdown() adds the following lines to .gitignore and .Rbuildignore (only the ones not already present in each file):

# .gitignore
_quarto/*
!_quarto/_freeze/
altdoc/freeze.rds
altdoc/pkgdown.yml
altdoc/quarto_website.yml
altdoc/index.md
altdoc/reference.qmd
altdoc/authors.qmd
altdoc/altdown.scss
altdoc/altdown-header.html
altdoc/altdown-after-body.html
altdoc/altdown-pre-render.R

# .Rbuildignore
^docs\$
^altdoc\$
^_quarto\$


The first four mirror what altdoc::setup_docs(tool = "quarto_website") adds, plus altdoc/pkgdown.yml, which altdoc::render_docs() rewrites on every build. The rest are the files build_site() generates.



Invisibly, the path to the altdoc/ directory.




pkg <- tempfile("examplepkg")
dir.create(pkg)
write(
  "Package: examplepkg\nVersion: 0.0.0.9000",
  file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION")
)
use_altdown(pkg)
list.files(file.path(pkg, "altdoc"))
#> [1] "altdown.yml"
unlink(pkg, recursive = TRUE)

title: Get started with altdown
text: altdown builds a pkgdown-style website for an R package with altdoc and Quarto. This guide sets up a package, builds its site, and publishes it on GitHub Pages.

title: Get started with altdown
text:
Set up
From the root of your package, run:
altdown::use_altdown()
This writes altdoc/altdown.yml, the one configuration file you edit, and adds the files the build generates to .gitignore and .Rbuildignore.

title: Get started with altdown
text:
Build the site
altdown::build_site()
altdoc::preview_docs()
build_site() builds the site into docs/, and altdoc::preview_docs() opens it in your browser.






Important



Examples in the man pages and code in the vignettes run against the installed version of your package, so install it before building, e.g. with devtools::install().


The site is built from what’s already in your package:

Home page: README.md, with a sidebar of links, the license, citation and developers taken from DESCRIPTION. Badges between <!-- badges: start --> and <!-- badges: end --> move into the sidebar.
Reference: one page per man/*.Rd file, and an index of them.
Get started: the vignette named after the package, like this one.
Articles: every other vignette, including those in vignettes/articles/.
Changelog: NEWS.md.

title: Get started with altdown
text:
Organize the reference index
By default the reference index lists every function in one section. To group them, edit the reference: field in altdoc/altdown.yml. It has the same shape as pkgdown’s:
reference:
  - title: Setting up
    contents:
      - use_altdown
  - title: Building
    contents:
      - starts_with("build_")
?build_site lists the other fields: articles: sets the order of the “Articles” menu, and quarto: changes the Quarto configuration, e.g. to add navbar links.

title: Get started with altdown
text:
Publish on GitHub Pages
altdoc can write a GitHub Actions workflow that builds the site and deploys it to the gh-pages branch on every push:
altdoc::setup_github_actions()
The workflow calls altdoc directly, so in .github/workflows/altdoc.yaml, change the “Build site” step to call altdown instead:
      - name: Build site
        run: |
          install.packages(".", repos = NULL, type = "source")
          install.packages("pak")
          pak::pak("BjarkeHautop/altdown")
          altdown::build_site(parallel = FALSE, freeze = FALSE)
        shell: Rscript {0}
Then, on GitHub, set the repository to serve Pages from the gh-pages branch (Settings → Pages).

title: altdown
text:
Browse source code
Report a bug



Full license
MIT + file LICENSE



Contributing guide



Citing altdown



Bjarke Hautop Kristensen
Author, maintainer



 

altdown is an R package that provides a theme for altdoc websites built with Quarto, styled to mirror the output of pkgdown (Bootstrap 5).


pkgdown can render Quarto vignettes, but it replaces Quarto’s styling with its own (theme: "none", minimal: TRUE). As a result, Quarto features such as callout blocks, code annotations and tabsets don’t render correctly; callouts, for instance, become plain blockquotes.
altdown builds on altdoc, which uses Quarto’s own rendering, and adds a pkgdown-style layout on top. You get:

full Quarto support;
a familiar pkgdown look;
links from your package’s functions to their reference page, with hover tooltips showing usage and a one-line summary.




Install from GitHub:
pak::pak("https://github.com/BjarkeHautop/altdown")



Browse around to see how it looks! If you like what you see, and want to use it for your own package, run:
altdown::use_altdown()
This writes altdoc/altdown.yml, with a reference: field that lists your package’s current functions in one section; edit it to group them however you’d like, in the same shape as pkgdown’s reference: field. It also gitignores the files the build generates.
Then build the site:
altdown::build_site()
A preview can then be viewed using altdoc::preview_docs().
The navbar is built from your vignettes: the one named after the package (or the only top-level one) becomes “Get started”, and the rest, including those in vignettes/articles/, go under “Articles”. See ?altdown::build_site for everything altdown.yml can configure.




jlbind

Using altdown for your package? Feel free to open a pull request adding it to this list.

title: Technical details
text: This article explains how altdown builds a site. altdown doesn’t render anything itself: altdoc converts the man pages and vignettes and renders them with Quarto, and altdown supplies the pkgdown-style layout around them.

title: Technical details
text:
How a build works
altdown::build_site() runs in three stages:

Before rendering, it writes a set of files into altdoc/. altdoc copies that folder into its Quarto project, so these files end up in the site.
During rendering, altdoc::render_docs() converts the Rd files to Quarto pages and renders the project. A pre-render script fixes up the man pages before Quarto sees them.
After rendering, it adds hover tooltips to the HTML in docs/.

Customizing a site by generating its source files and then calling altdoc::render_docs() is the approach altdoc itself recommends for Quarto1.
The only file you edit is altdoc/altdown.yml. Everything else in altdoc/ is rewritten on every build, and gitignored by altdown::use_altdown():
altdoc/
├── altdown.yml                # configuration, edited by hand
├── quarto_website.yml         # Quarto configuration (navbar, footer, theme)
├── index.md                   # home page
├── reference.qmd              # function reference index
├── authors.qmd                # authors and citation page
├── altdown.scss               # pkgdown-style theme on top of Quarto's HTML
├── altdown-header.html        # dark-mode default
├── altdown-after-body.html    # navbar alignment
└── altdown-pre-render.R       # fixes up altdoc's man pages

title: Technical details
text:
Before rendering

The home page
altdoc’s home page is an index.md that includes README.md. altdoc copies altdoc/ into its Quarto project after importing the README, so the altdoc/index.md that build_site() writes takes its place. It holds the README’s content next to a pkgdown-style sidebar, with links, the license, the citation, the developers and the README’s badges.
The sidebar is a .column-margin div, Quarto’s margin column, so on a narrow screen it moves below the content as Quarto’s layout intends.
A README image can have a light and a dark version, given GitHub’s way, as a <picture> with a <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)">. On the site that would follow the operating system’s setting instead of the site’s own light/dark toggle, so each such <picture> becomes one <img> per theme, using Quarto’s .light-content and .dark-content classes.


The reference index
altdoc has no way to group and order the function index, like pkgdown’s reference: field (etiennebacher/altdoc#326). So altdoc/altdown.yml has a reference: field of its own, in the same shape as pkgdown’s:
reference:
1  - title: Building the site
2    desc: >
      Set up a package, then build its site.
    contents:
3      - use_altdown
4      - starts_with("build_")

1

Each entry becomes a section of the index, with this heading.

2

An optional description, shown under the heading.

3

A topic, by any of its \alias{} names.

4

A selector, as in pkgdown: starts_with(), ends_with(), contains(), matches(), has_concept(), has_keyword(), - to exclude and c() to combine.


build_site() resolves these against the \name{} and \alias{} entries in man/*.Rd and writes the index to altdoc/reference.qmd.


The navbar and footer
altdoc/quarto_website.yml is generated in full. The navbar links the “Get started” vignette, the reference index, the other vignettes under “Articles” and the changelog. The footer has pkgdown’s “Developed by …” text, built from Authors@R.






TipChanging the Quarto configuration



A quarto: field in altdown.yml is merged over the generated configuration. A list of entries, like the navbar’s items, is added to; any other setting is replaced, and ~ removes it. For example, to add a link to the navbar and fold code blocks:
quarto:
  website:
    navbar:
      right:
        - text: Blog
          href: https://example.com
  format:
    html:
      code-fold: true

title: Technical details
text:
During rendering: the man pages
altdoc converts each man/*.Rd file to a .qmd page during altdoc::render_docs() and renders the Quarto project straight after, so build_site() can’t edit those pages beforehand. Instead, altdown-pre-render.R runs as a Quarto pre-render script, inside that render. It makes the pages look like pkgdown’s:

Usage becomes an R code block, so it’s syntax-highlighted and gets a copy button, like the examples.
Inline code becomes Markdown code spans. Pandoc would otherwise turn a " inside <code> into a curly quote, and a trailing backslash would escape the closing </code>.
Examples that are run show their output in the same block, prefixed with #>. The library() call altdoc adds for the package itself is hidden.
Examples that aren’t run (\dontrun{}) become plain code blocks, so their pages render without starting an R session2.

title: Technical details
text:
After rendering: hover tooltips
Quarto’s code-link option links function names in code blocks to their documentation with downlit, but downlit doesn’t know about this site, so it can’t link the package’s own functions to their man pages here. So after rendering, build_site() goes through every page in docs/ and links each reference to one of the package’s own functions, in a code block or in inline code, to its man page. Hovering over it shows a tooltip with the function’s usage and the first sentence of its description, taken from man/*.Rd.
Try it: hover over build_site() or use_altdown(). To build without tooltips, use build_site(tooltips = FALSE).






Note



The tooltip shows the first sentence of the description, cut off at 200 characters. build_site() warns when a sentence is longer, so you can shorten it.

title: Technical details
text:
Matching the pkgdown look
altdown.scss is a Quarto theme layer, added on top of Quarto’s own light and dark themes:
theme:
  light: [default, altdown.scss]
  dark: [darkly, altdown.scss]
It is based on pkgdown’s pkgdown.scss, with the selectors adapted to Quarto’s HTML. It:

limits the navbar to a centered, fixed-width container;
puts the navbar items (title, links, search, GitHub icon) in pkgdown’s order;
styles the margin sidebar and the reference index to look like pkgdown’s.

Two things can’t be done in CSS alone:

Dark mode by default. Quarto’s light/dark toggle always starts new visitors on the light theme. altdown-header.html starts them on the dark theme if their system prefers it, unless they’ve used the toggle before.
Aligning the navbar title with the body text. Quarto’s home page uses a different layout from the other pages, so the body’s left edge isn’t in the same place on every page. altdown-after-body.html measures it once the page has loaded and adjusts the navbar’s padding to match.

title: Technical details
text:
Footnotes


See altdoc’s customization vignette.↩︎
A ```{r} chunk makes Quarto render the page with knitr, even with eval=FALSE, and that starts a separate R session per page.↩︎

text:
Builds the package website into docs/ with altdoc::render_docs(), styled to mirror pkgdown. Before rendering it generates, from the package sources and altdoc/altdown.yml:



build_site(path = ".", tooltips = TRUE, ...)






path


Path to the package root.




tooltips


Logical. Link references to the package’s own functions (in code blocks and inline code) to their reference page, with a hover tooltip showing the function’s usage and the first sentence of its description?




...


Passed on to altdoc::render_docs(), e.g. freeze or parallel.








the navbar, with a "Get started" link, the function reference, an "Articles" menu and the changelog;


the home page, built from README.md plus a pkgdown-style sidebar (links, license, citation, developers and the README’s badges). An image with light and dark versions, given as a <picture> with a <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"> as on GitHub, follows the site’s light/dark toggle;


the grouped function reference index;


the "Authors and Citation" page.


These generated files are written to altdoc/ (which altdoc copies into its Quarto project), so they’re gitignored by use_altdown(). README.md itself is never modified.



Invisibly, the path to the built site.



altdoc/altdown.yml (created by use_altdown()) can contain:


reference: groups the function reference index, in the same shape as pkgdown’s reference: field. contents entries can be a topic alias or a selector: starts_with(), ends_with(), contains(), matches(), has_concept(), has_keyword(), - to exclude, and c() to combine. Without it, every topic is listed in one section.


articles: the order of the "Articles" navbar menu, as vignette paths relative to vignettes/ without extension (e.g. articles/details). Without it, every vignette other than the "Get started" one is listed, top-level vignettes first, then those in vignettes/articles/.


quarto: settings merged over the generated Quarto configuration. Settings are merged key by key: a list of entries (e.g. the navbar’s left: or right: items) is added to, any other value is replaced, and ~ removes a setting. For example, to add a navbar link:

quarto:
  website:
    navbar:
      right:
        - text: Blog
          href: https://example.com




The "Get started" link points to the vignette named after the package, or to the only top-level vignette if there is just one.
